name: Project Arsenal
teaser: Project Arsenal is a large-scale ammunition, crafting, trader, and quest expansion for Single Player Tarkov, built around realistic progression, deep weapon specialization, and experimental ballistic projects.

⚠️ REQUIRED DEPENDENCIES — READ BEFORE INSTALLING

Do not rely solely on the compatibility information displayed by The Forge under “Dependencies”. The displayed SPT compatibility status of individual dependencies may be incorrect, incomplete or outdated.

Project Arsenal 0.0.1 was built and tested for SPT 4.0.13 using the exact dependency versions listed below.

All dependencies are mandatory:

  • TraderGen 2.2.0
  • AmmoGen 2.3.0
  • ItemGen 1.5.0
  • Map Editor Lite 2.0.2
  • WTT ServerCommonLib 2.0.23
  • WTT-ContentBackport 1.0.7
  • WTT-Armory 2.0.5
  • MassivesoftCore 1.0.2
  • MassivesoftWeapons 1.1.1

Install these versions before reporting startup errors, missing items, broken quests or unavailable recipes. Using newer, older or otherwise incompatible dependency versions may prevent Project Arsenal from loading correctly.

⚠️ SPT VERSION NOTICE

Project Arsenal is currently built for SPT 4.0.13.

An update to SPT 4.1.1 will be released as soon as all mandatory dependencies have received compatible updates and Project Arsenal has passed compatibility testing.

Until then, Project Arsenal should not be assumed to work correctly on SPT 4.1.1, regardless of any compatibility labels displayed by The Forge.

Project Arsenal

Ammunition is no longer a shopping list. It is progression.

“Factory ammunition is only a starting point. A man who cannot understand the starting point should not be trusted with the destination.” — Mikhail Volkov, The Alchemist

Project Arsenal is a large-scale, quest-driven ammunition, crafting and progression expansion for SPT.

Instead of simply adding a new “best round” to every caliber, Project Arsenal gives cartridges distinct jobs. Some are designed for precision. Some reshape recoil for automatic fire. Some trade velocity for discretion. Others sacrifice economy, weapon life or comfort in exchange for extreme terminal performance.

Every loading is a compromise—and learning when that compromise is useful is the heart of the mod.

Vanilla ammunition remains relevant throughout the entire game. Existing cartridges are not obsolete loot: they become shootable crafting ingredients used as donor loads for refined, specialized and experimental ammunition at the Workbench.

Alpha Content at a Glance

  • 214 custom cartridges covering 32 calibers
  • 4 custom hand grenades
  • 4 custom grenade-launcher rounds
  • 222 individual Workbench recipes
  • 107 fully written quests
  • 49 bespoke in-raid quest artifacts across 10 locations
  • 22 separate Prototype Authorizations
  • Quest-locked ammunition recipes and trader assortments
  • Fixed-batch access to restricted factory donor ammunition
  • Quest-locked weapons, optics, mounts and specialist equipment
  • Early-, mid- and late-game progression across Workbench levels 1–3

The Alpha includes:

  • Real-world ammunition missing from the base game
  • Plausible military, civilian, hunting and specialist loadings
  • Carefully designed handloads and refined donor cartridges
  • Fictional Soviet and Russian prototype projects
  • TerraGroup Black Projects
  • Dedicated stats, descriptions, recipes, costs, unlock conditions and lore for every new munition
  • Reworked interpretations of 7.62×51 mm M118LR and 7.62×54 mm R Tungsten Carbide AP
  • New tactical roles for calibers and weapons that normally lose relevance during progression

Workbench Distribution

Workbench Level Recipes
Workbench 1 52
Workbench 2 88
Workbench 3 82
Total 222

Recipes are not handed to the player all at once. Completing the appropriate quest permanently unlocks its blueprint.

Progress comes from knowledge and field work—not from reaching a trader level and buying unlimited stacks from a shelf.

Meet the Alchemist

Mikhail Volkov, better known as The Alchemist, is a former Soviet ballistic engineer with decades of experience, very little patience and an unhealthy familiarity with chamber pressure.

He becomes available after completing Jaeger’s “Acquaintance” quest and accompanies the player from early Workbench experiments to classified Soviet archives and TerraGroup’s most dangerous research programs.

The Alchemist is not a conventional ammunition trader.

His assortment focuses on:

  • Propellants
  • Tools and components
  • Restricted donor ammunition
  • Carefully controlled barter opportunities
  • Quest-gated specialist weapons
  • Optics and mounting equipment

He does not exist to sell unlimited quantities of Project Arsenal ammunition. He teaches the player how to manufacture it, provides restricted factory ammunition when progression requires it and expects every useful lesson to be proven in the field.

His storyline combines practical ammunition work, dry Russian humor, field trials, archive recovery and an escalating investigation into projects that should probably have remained buried.

Quest and Progression Structure

Project Arsenal is designed to feel like an expansion of Tarkov’s existing progression rather than a separate cheat menu.

Questline Prefix Quests
Main Story M 12
Specializations S 21
Legendary Projects L 44
TerraGroup T 30
Total 107

Main Story

The early quests introduce:

  • Cartridge construction
  • Donor ammunition
  • Civilian and hunting ammunition
  • Practical service loads
  • Workbench progression
  • Restricted components
  • Heavy and experimental ammunition concepts

These recipes provide meaningful alternatives without bypassing the normal early-game struggle.

Weapon and Caliber Specializations

As the questline develops, the player gains access to dedicated specialization branches for:

  • Pistol ammunition
  • 4.6×30 mm and 5.7×28 mm PDWs
  • Intermediate rifles
  • Full-power rifle cartridges
  • Suppressed weapons
  • Shotguns
  • Precision rifles
  • Heavy weapons
  • Grenade launchers
  • Special-purpose ammunition

Specialization quests introduce related loading families such as:

  • Precision
  • Control
  • Modernized
  • High Velocity
  • Subsonic
  • Refined

Each cartridge retains a distinct purpose instead of becoming a simple statistical upgrade.

Legendary Projects

The Legendary branch follows fictional Soviet and Russian prototype projects, unusual specialist programs, refined foreign designs and experimental grenades.

These projects are original Project Arsenal creations. They are not presented as real historical ammunition programs.

Their names, engineering problems and archive lore are fictional, although many of the underlying ballistic concepts are inspired by real projectile technology and military research.

Two-Stage Prototype Progression

Each of the 22 Legendary Projects follows the same basic structure:

  1. Recover the project’s files, drawings, test reports or physical evidence.
  2. Receive a unique Prototype Authorization, produce a limited trial batch and prove the design in the field.

Only after the field trial is complete does the permanent recipe become available.

Legendary ammunition is powerful, rare and expensive—but deliberately specialized. These cartridges are progression capstones, not universal replacements for everything below them.

The first Legendary questline, Project Sokol for .366 TKM, becomes available at player level 15 after completing M05 – The Journeyman’s Bench.

Every later Legendary project requires the appropriate completed Specialization quest, tying recovered prototype designs to mastery of their caliber or weapon class.

TerraGroup Black Projects

The late-game investigation opens TerraGroup’s compartmentalized ammunition programs.

These include:

  • High-pressure PDW concepts
  • Advanced penetrators
  • Duplex and flechette designs
  • Heavy anti-materiel projects
  • Experimental explosive payloads
  • The Mjölnir-derived technology behind Naglfar

TerraGroup ammunition pushes performance far beyond conventional service requirements, but its advantages come with severe costs:

  • Scarce donor ammunition
  • Expensive components
  • Tiny production batches
  • Heavy recoil
  • Excessive heat
  • Accelerated weapon wear
  • Highly specialized behavior
  • Questionable safety margins

The 30-quest TerraGroup storyline begins at player level 40 and requires completion of M12 – The Master’s Examination.

In the Alchemist’s words, some of it is less ammunition engineering and more:

“A pact with the devil in a brass case.”

Real Quest Artifacts

The Russian archive and TerraGroup investigations use 49 custom in-raid quest artifacts across:

  • Ground Zero
  • Customs
  • Woods
  • Factory
  • Shoreline
  • Interchange
  • Reserve
  • Lighthouse
  • Streets of Tarkov
  • The Lab

Quest artifacts follow a consistent set of rules:

  • They spawn only while the relevant quest is active.
  • The item is guaranteed to exist somewhere inside the hinted landmark area.
  • One of several nearby anchors is selected.
  • The artifact enters the quest inventory.
  • The artifact is lost on death.
  • It cannot be sold or listed on the Flea Market.
  • It does not appear as ordinary loot.
  • The player must survive and extract with the recovered material.

Quest dialogue provides an approximate location and enough context to begin the search without reducing each recovery mission to a glowing objective marker.

Giving Forgotten Weapons a New Purpose

Project Arsenal does not focus only on popular assault-rifle calibers.

One of its central goals is to make overlooked cartridges and niche weapons relevant again by giving them several distinct roles instead of one short-lived gimmick.

.366 TKM

.366 TKM develops from an early-game compromise into a complete ammunition family.

Its progression includes:

  • Match ammunition
  • Premium civilian loads
  • Subsonic ammunition
  • High Velocity ammunition
  • Specialized armor-defeating designs

This allows the VPO platforms to remain useful as hunting rifles, suppressed weapons and precision tools.

At the end of that path waits Project Sokol—a Legendary experiment that asks how much performance can be extracted from a civilian caliber and a rifle most soldiers would dismiss.

KS-23 and 23×75 mm R

The KS-23 receives a broad family of specialist ammunition:

  • HE-FI
  • AP-HE
  • Mini-HESH
  • APDS
  • FAPDS
  • TP-T
  • Refined Volna concepts

Depending on the shell, the KS-23 can be configured for breaching, armor damage, direct-impact precision, fragmentation or specialist utility.

Conventional Shotguns

12/70 and 20/70 shotguns also receive carefully differentiated ammunition.

Project Arsenal adds:

  • Precision slugs
  • Barrier-oriented cartridges
  • Specialized buckshot
  • Hunting and civilian loads
  • Unusual tactical ammunition

The goal is not to make every weapon equally powerful. It is to give more weapons a credible reason to leave the stash.

Familiar Cartridges with More Credible Ballistics

Project Arsenal also includes revised interpretations of two well-known cartridges.

7.62×51 mm M118LR

M118LR returns to its intended role as a precision-oriented long-range match cartridge.

Its value comes from:

  • Consistency
  • External ballistics
  • Accuracy
  • Retained long-range performance

It is not treated as an implausible universal armor-piercing cartridge.

7.62×54 mm R Tungsten Carbide AP

Tungsten Carbide AP remains a formidable specialist armor-piercing cartridge, but its damage, penetration and overall performance have been brought into a more credible relationship with its construction and caliber.

Both cartridges remain valuable high-end tools without becoming stat-inflated shortcuts that make every other loading irrelevant.

Ammunition Philosophy

There is no single “best” Project Arsenal cartridge.

Each loading is balanced through a combination of:

  • Flesh damage
  • Penetration
  • Armor damage
  • Muzzle velocity
  • Long-range behavior
  • Accuracy modifiers
  • Recoil modifiers
  • Fragmentation
  • Ricochet chance
  • Bleeding potential
  • Heat generation
  • Durability burn
  • Donor-ammunition availability
  • Component cost
  • Production time
  • Batch size
  • Workbench requirement
  • Quest placement

A cartridge that dominates one task should create a meaningful disadvantage somewhere else.

A controllable loading may surrender velocity. A high-velocity cartridge may punish the weapon. A precision load may be wasted in close-range automatic fire. A Legendary penetrator may be too expensive to use as general-purpose ammunition.

Project Arsenal expands the toolbox. It does not replace it with one hammer.

Ammunition Naming Guide

Project Arsenal’s names describe a cartridge’s design goal, not a simple quality tier.

A suffix does not automatically mean “better.” It tells the player what was changed and which compromise the loading is built around.

Real-World, Factory and Service Ammunition

Existing military, law-enforcement, sporting or experimental ammunition missing from the base game.

These cartridges normally retain their real designation.

Premium

Higher-quality civilian or hunting ammunition assembled for improved consistency or terminal behavior.

“Premium” does not automatically mean armor-piercing.

Match

Ammunition produced with tighter tolerances, selected components and an emphasis on repeatable accuracy.

Match ammunition is built for precision, not necessarily maximum damage or penetration.

-P — Precision

A loading optimized for consistency, dispersion and deliberate fire.

Examples include FMJ-P and Whisper-P.

-C — Control

A cartridge tuned to reshape recoil impulse and improve controllability during rapid, burst or automatic fire.

Examples include M80-C, M62-C and BT-C.

Reduced recoil may cost velocity, energy or penetration.

-M — Modernized

An established cartridge updated through revised projectile construction, propellant selection or loading methods while preserving its original role.

Examples include M855-M, M995-M and BT-M.

Modernized ammunition may generate additional pressure, heat, wear or cost.

-HV — High Velocity

A faster loading intended to produce a flatter trajectory, shorter flight time or improved impact behavior.

Additional velocity commonly produces more recoil, pressure, heat or durability burn.

Subsonic

Ammunition kept below the speed of sound for suppressed use and a reduced ballistic signature.

Subsonic loads usually offer improved control and discretion in exchange for a more curved trajectory, lower retained energy or reduced penetration.

-R — Refined

An existing cartridge used as a donor load and carefully reworked by the Alchemist.

Powder charges, projectiles and assembly tolerances are selected and controlled to sharpen a specific role.

Examples include Match-R, M8 API-R and Raufoss-R.

Special Purpose

Barrier, tracer, incendiary, frangible, sabot, duplex, flechette and other role-specific ammunition.

Conventional abbreviations such as AP, API, APIT, HE, HEI and APDS retain their normal meaning.

Named and Legendary Projects

Fictional Soviet or Russian prototype ammunition created for Project Arsenal.

Examples include:

  • Sokol
  • Voron
  • Freight Train
  • Molot
  • Perun

These designs are inspired by real ballistic concepts but are not historical cartridges.

TG and TerraGroup Black Projects

Fictional late-game ammunition created under TerraGroup’s compartmentalized programs.

These cartridges explore extreme pressure, advanced penetrators, unusual payloads and questionable safety margins.

Some ammunition combines multiple design markers where appropriate. The complete item name and description always take priority.

Grenade and Launcher Expansion

Project Arsenal extends its progression beyond conventional cartridges.

Hand Grenades

  • RGO-92 “Groza”
  • RGN-93 “Kapkan”
  • TG-MF9 “Hailstorm”
  • TG-SF4 “Black Ice”

Grenade-Launcher Rounds

  • 40×53 mm OFK-93 “Metel”
  • 40×53 mm OFS-94 “Kuvalda”
  • 40×46 mm XM1187 “Porcupine”
  • 40×46 mm XM1192 “Shattercloud”

These follow the same design principles as the main ammunition expansion:

  • Dedicated quests
  • Workbench recipes
  • Limited production batches
  • Strong individual identities
  • Deliberate progression placement

Black Ice becomes available only after the technologies behind Shattercloud and Hailstorm have been recovered.

All three compatible 40 mm grenade-launcher platforms can also be obtained from the Alchemist through expensive, quest-locked barter trades.

Crafting, Economy and Availability

  • Project Arsenal ammunition is primarily crafted, not purchased.
  • Recipes use believable donor cartridges and Tarkov crafting materials.
  • The Alchemist supplies knowledge and components rather than unlimited finished ammunition.
  • Unlocking a recipe also unlocks a fixed-batch offer for its required factory donor ammunition.
  • Loot-only donor ammunition costs between ₽5,000 and ₽25,000 per round or grenade.
  • Donor ammunition normally available from traders or the Flea Market costs the Flea Market reference price plus 25%.
  • Every restricted offer is limited to one fixed batch per trader restock.
  • Selected real-world factory ammunition may appear in extremely rare ammunition boxes.
  • Handcrafted, Legendary and TerraGroup ammunition remains outside ordinary loot pools.
  • High-end experimental items are Flea-restricted where required.
  • Crafting time, cost and output scale with the role and performance of the ammunition.

Controlled Donor-Ammunition Access

Whenever a Project Arsenal recipe requires factory ammunition as a donor load, completing the quest that unlocks the recipe also unlocks a corresponding fixed-batch offer at the Alchemist.

This prevents a learned blueprint from becoming unusable because its required donor ammunition has no reliable source.

If the donor cartridge is loot-only, its price is set between ₽5,000 and ₽25,000 per round or grenade, depending on caliber and performance.

If it is normally available from another trader or through the Flea Market, the Alchemist charges the Flea Market reference value plus a 25% premium.

His offer provides dependable access, while the surcharge keeps normal trader and Flea acquisition economically preferable.

Version and Required Dependencies

The initial Alpha is built and tested for:

SPT 4.0.13

Project Arsenal requires all of the following dependencies:

  • TraderGen 2.2.0
  • AmmoGen 2.3.0
  • ItemGen 1.5.0
  • Map Editor Lite 2.0.2
  • WTT ServerCommonLib 2.0.23

These are mandatory requirements, not optional compatibility recommendations.

Project Arsenal uses their frameworks, items and weapon platforms throughout its ammunition, crafting and quest progression.

Please use the dependency versions listed for the current release. Requirements may change with future SPT updates.

Alpha Notice

Project Arsenal is entering public testing as an Alpha.

The complete initial progression and content structure is present, but the following may change in response to testing:

  • Cartridge values
  • Crafting costs
  • Production quantities
  • Quest objectives
  • Quest pacing
  • Trader prices
  • Compatibility
  • Progression placement
  • Item locations

The Alpha currently uses compatible existing game assets for much of its ammunition and ordnance.

Dedicated cartridge models, grenade models, improved textures and additional visual assets are planned for later development.

When reporting a problem, please include:

  • The affected quest, cartridge or recipe
  • A description of what happened
  • Steps to reproduce the issue
  • The relevant server-log section whenever possible

Community Feedback and Bug Reports

Project Arsenal’s Alpha will be shaped by the people actually playing it.

Feedback on progression, recipe costs, cartridge balance, quest pacing and compatibility problems is extremely valuable.

  • Separate projectiles, propellant and primers
  • Additional calibers
  • Compatibility patches
  • Continued balancing
  • Further quest dialogue and lore improvements
  • Additional localization support

A Note from the Developer

Project Arsenal is my first mod project.

What started as an attempt to give Tarkov’s overlooked ammunition more purpose grew into something much larger: a complete crafting progression, a new trader and an investigation spanning fictional Russian prototype projects and TerraGroup Black Projects.

I have put an enormous amount of care into the research, balancing, recipes and writing, but an Alpha of this size will inevitably have rough edges.

Constructive criticism, detailed bug reports and honest player feedback will help Project Arsenal become the mod I want it to be.

Thank you for giving my first project a place in your SPT installation.
